newsitem.title: UK: Rail watchdog in clampdown on ticket overcharging.
newsitem.headline: Rail watchdog in clampdown on ticket overcharging.

text.p: The UK's rail industry watchdog announced moves to clamp down on overcharging by privatised rail companies on Wednesday by demanding improvements to information available to customers on ticketing and services.

John Swift, the rail regulator, wrote to the managing directors of the 25 train operating companies, or passenger rail franchises, urging them to improve their peformance on providing accurate information to customers or face tough fines.

The move follows a fallback in consumer confidence in the ticketing system and reports from groups like the Consumers Association which has showed 10 percent of customers were overcharged by an average 24 pounds per ticket.

The regulator rebuffed calls by some groups for a unified ticketing agency, but warned "Accurate and impartial retailing is essential if passengers are to be able to use the railway with confidence. It is clear that operators can and must do much better in this respect."

The Office of Passenger Rail Franchising, which regulates the awarding of passenger rail franchises to private sector bidders, welcomed the clampdown which will include anonymous inspections as "good business sense."

But the Save Our Railways (SOR) pressure gorup called for the rail regulator Swift to beef up his demands with huge fines. Jonathan Bray, spokesman, said "The regulator should back up his strong words with strong action. Companies that consistently cheat customers by not giving them the best and cheapest fare deal should be fined at least 500,000 pounds."
